rationale: The DESeq2 negative-binomial Wald test with a single condition factor is a valid (if slower than limma-voom) fit to an unpaired, single-batch 60v60 cohort, and the plan correctly centers effect size, though it uses post hoc |shrunken log2FC| >= 1 filtering rather than an in-test threshold (lfcThreshold/TREAT), which is exactly the distinction the question demands at n=120. QC is concrete (library sizes, zero-count genes, VST PCA colored by condition, an explicit >3SD outlier rule, resolution of the 121-vs-120 mismatch) but omits a sex check against XIST/Y genes and any search for hidden structure beyond the cell-composition check. The weakest point is filtering: the plan leans entirely on DESeq2's independent filtering at the results stage and never states a minimal expression pre-filter, so the tested gene set is undefined up front; normalization is handled correctly with size factors on raw counts. The design formula is described in prose only, with no explicit ~condition formula, reference level, or contrast direction. Enrichment is strong on universe (the tested genes) and offers both ORA and preranked fgsea on named collections, but lacks collection versions and a gene-set size window; reporting covers methods, thresholds, category counts, and deconvolution caveats but not software versions.
